items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: I always say if you blindfold somebody — I mean is it they’re the best black guitarist, the best Italian-American guitarist.

ctx.x: Good point. I remember Marian McPartland saying a similar thing — like with her wonderful accent you know, pointing out that oh she’s the finest woman jazz pianist.

Right, right, right, right, right. Yeah I mean in this art form hopefully it is about the music. We want it to be about the music. And I always say if you blindfold somebody — I mean is it they’re the best black guitarist, the best Italian-American guitarist. Is that how © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

we’re listening to music? It’s the best male guitarist, it’s the best female. I mean come on. Like life is complicated enough. Let’s just listen and play the music. Either you can play or you can’t play. That’s what it comes down to for me.

items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: I used to see him a lot. I would see Tal Farlow, I saw Herb Ellis. They would come through because of Joe Negri from Mr. Rogers Neighborhood.

ctx.x: Well said. Was there a particular artist and even beyond that a particular LP that put you on the jazz path?

Yeah, well you know I’m from the Pittsburgh area and there was a radio station back when you had way more independent radio stations, WYEP, and they had all kinds of — it was public access radio. And you know I just listened to all kinds of things there. And I turned it on and I heard Sonny Rollins. And then I heard Charlie Parker. And then I heard Wes Montgomery. And then I just was hooked. It was an addiction from there. So then I started — my mother actually — at the time I was playing in a rock band and my…
Yeah. Did you have to go out and then get a different kind of guitar?
